title: Why You Forget Things Walking Through A Door

scenes.say: You walk into a room, and instantly forget why. That's not you. It's the door.
Scientists call it the doorway effect.
scenes.heading: IT HAS A NAME

scenes.say: In one study, people carried objects through rooms. Those who walked through a doorway forgot more than those who walked the same distance in one room.
scenes.heading: THE EXPERIMENT

scenes.say: The theory: your brain files memories into chapters. A doorway tells it a new chapter just started.
scenes.heading: WHY?

scenes.say: So the thought you had in the last room gets filed away.
Wildest part? Even imagining walking through a door made people forget more.
scenes.heading: EVEN WEIRDER

scenes.say: Not every study finds it, so scientists still debate it. But the fix is easy: go back through the door. It often comes right back.
scenes.heading: THE FIX

scenes.say: Does this happen to you every day?
